query: What robust training schedules, error-mitigation rollouts, and fallback criteria will decide when to remain on classical emulation versus proceed to noisy hardware fine-tuning?

response.query: What robust training schedules, error-mitigation rollouts, and fallback criteria will decide when to remain on classical emulation versus proceed to noisy hardware fine-tuning?
response.answer: Use classical emulation until error rates are below 1% and performance stabilizes; switch to noisy hardware fine-tuning if performance plateaus or diverges. Fallback criteria include reverting to classical if hardware errors exceed 5%.
